name: Canvas court sneaker
summary: The cotton canvas shoe on a vulcanised rubber sole. It is a white or navy high-top or low-top with a toe cap and a thin foxing strip. It was first made for basketball in 1917.

philosophy.core_thesis: A court shoe is cheap cloth on a cured rubber sole, so it grips the floor and costs little; its plainness is the style.
design_principles: Cut the upper in cotton canvas of 400 to 600 gsm and stitch it to a rubber foxing strip.
Cure the sole with the upper in a vulcanising oven, so that the rubber bonds to the canvas.
Cap the toe in rubber, and set a round ankle patch on the inside of a high-top.
Use 8 pairs of eyelets with a flat cotton lace.
Print one small mark on the ankle patch; keep the rest plain.
Set the sole at 2 to 3 cm, flat, with a diamond or herringbone tread.
Leave the canvas free of coating, so that it can fade and crease.
anti_patterns: A padded, cushioned midsole with air units
Large printed logos across the side

silhouette.shape: A light, low-sided shoe with a flat sole, a rubber toe cap and a round toe.
silhouette.line: A straight line along the foxing strip; the high-top rises to the ankle bone.
silhouette.fit: Loose and flat, held by the lace; the canvas gives and takes the shape of the foot.
silhouette.proportion: Sole 2 to 3 cm; high-top shaft 12 cm above the sole; toe cap one quarter of the shoe length.
rules: Keep the sole flat and white.
Run the foxing strip round the whole sole.
Use a toe cap and an ankle patch only.
Let the canvas crease and darken with wear.

fabrics.rule: Use cotton canvas for the upper and cured rubber for the sole, the toe cap and the foxing strip. Use leather for a premium upper only.

methods: canvas upper cut and stitched flat
rubber foxing strip applied to the upper
herringbone tread moulded in the sole
construction.closures: A flat cotton lace through eight pairs of metal eyelets.
construction.details: A round ankle patch, a toe cap, a foxing strip with a stripe, a vulcanised rubber sole and a cotton lining.

surface.pattern: Plain white, black or navy canvas; a screen-printed ankle patch; a single stripe on the foxing.
surface.gloss: Canvas at 2–5 GU; the rubber sole at 15–30 GU.
surface.wear: The shoe looks right when the canvas is grubby, creased and frayed at the toe cap; a clean pair looks new but not wrong.

palette.strategy: Optical white, black and navy, with one colour for a team or a season.

making.scale: Factory made, by the million, in a few widths and in one cheap grade.
making.signs: A smooth foxing line, a bonded toe cap, a flat tread and a cotton lace.

emotion.target_response: A feeling of ease and youth: a shoe for play that asks for no care.

use_cases: a film costume for the 1930s to the 1960s
a product image prompt for a canvas shoe
a school or team uniform shoe
avoid_when: the brief wants a leather dress shoe
the brief wants a technical running shoe

modifiers.how: Swap the canvas for nylon mesh and the flat sole for a foam midsole with a waffle outsole.
Move to leather, add a bold colour block and a printed brand mark, and raise the sole.

ornament_level.note: A court shoe carries a printed patch and a stripe, and nothing else.
